//: Azure Container Apps scale rule for Orleans.Lattice.Scaling (issue #1188).
//scraper: A 'custom' scale rule of type 'metrics-api' polls the app's /lattice/scale endpoint and reads the scalar at valueLocation 'scaleValue'. KEDA (which backs ACA custom scale rules) divides the scraped value by targetValue to derive the desired replica count.
//placement: This sample shows the full properties.template.scale shape for a Microsoft.App/containerApps resource (api-version 2024-03-01 or later); copy the scale object or its rules into your existing resource.

metadata.//targetValue: The per-replica pressure the pool is held at. scaleValue is the dominant pressure (0.0 to 1.0) times the current replica count, so it never exceeds that count, and desiredReplicas = ceil(scaleValue / targetValue): targetValue must be below 1 for the pool to grow ('1' could only hold or shrink it). '0.5' asks for twice the current count at full saturation.
metadata.//url: Point this at the in-cluster address of a silo that mapped MapLatticeScalingSignal(). The path must match LatticeScalingSignalOptions.EndpointPath (default /lattice/scale).
metadata.//unsafeSsl: Set 'true' only when scraping a self-signed HTTPS endpoint in-cluster; prefer plain HTTP on a private network.
metadata.//pollingInterval-note: Polling cadence is configured on the ACA scale rule host (KEDA pollingInterval, default 30s). Keep it at or above LatticeScalingSignalOptions.SampleInterval so repeated scrapes do not just read the same cached sample.
metadata.//stabilizationWindow-note: KEDA/HPA scale-down stabilization (default 300s) holds the replica count at its recent maximum before scaling in. Because scaleValue is already EWMA-smoothed and gated on the producer side, choose a stabilization window deliberately; stacking a long HPA window on top of a long Lattice scale-in gate makes scale-in lag twice.
